headline: High-risk shared-workspace and filesystem-write pairing creates prompt-injection, data-leakage, and git-state conflict exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can call APIs and read/write the filesystem, while Roo Code reads workspace files, uses MCP, and runs browsers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGPT writes attacker-controlled text into shared files that Roo Code later treats as trusted input. The shared filesystem path is documented on Roo Code; AutoGPT’s file surface is documented too.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes untrusted content into a workspace file that Roo Code later reads as instructions
IF Roo Code is configured to ingest file contents or MCP output without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP for the Roo Code session
Mark shared files as data-only and never as prompts
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on AutoGPT output
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code explicitly reads and writes VS Code workspace files and handles model-provider API keys; AutoGPT has filesystem access and API-call capability. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent’s context into the other’s outputs or external API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF sensitive files or secrets are present in that workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace content to a configured model API
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict Roo Code to a redacted subset of files
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses; Roo Code can execute shell, write files, and modify git state, with shared state via filesystem across instances. That is a direct write-conflict pathway on the same workspace and git metadata, and the rubric treats unrestricted overlapping filesystem write plus git modification as high risk. No locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or workspace
IF either agent writes files while the other is active
IF git operations occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate clone
Pause one agent before the other edits the repo
Avoid concurrent git commits from both agents
Use a lock file around workspace mutations
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and browser output, while AutoGPT can generate files and shell-driven artifacts. If Roo Code treats AutoGPT’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or external actions without verification. The profiles show no built-in cross-agent verification step, but they also do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes AutoGPT-produced files as source-of-truth
IF Roo Code executes edits or browser actions based on those files without review
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Compare AutoGPT output against original sources
Limit AutoGPT to draft-only artifacts
Use a checksum or diff review step
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools, and neither profile states regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and workspace files; AutoGPT touches the filesystem and APIs. A compliance issue is only plausible if regulated data is placed into the shared workspace or sent to a noncompliant model endpoint, so the pathway is narrower than the operational risks.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send that data to an external model API
IF the chosen endpoint lacks the required compliance coverage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a compliant model endpoint only
Redact sensitive fields before prompting
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data
